facts.text: Clover incorporated in 1895 thanks to the railroad, then disincorporated in 1998 when a shrinking tax base made town governance unsustainable.
Black Walnut plantation near Clover earned a spot on the National Register of Historic Places in 1991 for its well‑preserved 19th‑century architecture.
Henrietta Lacks, raised on a Clover tobacco farm, unknowingly supplied the HeLa cell line that revolutionized cancer research and vaccine development.
By the early 1800s Clover had become a crossroads hamlet, anchored by the Clover Baptist Church founded in 1812.
The town’s proximity to the 1864 Battle of Staunton River Bridge placed it on the periphery of one of Halifax County’s few direct Civil War engagements.
